Altered mental status upon awakening suggests either an acute structural, metabolic, toxic, or epileptic process. Hypoglycemia is top-ranked due to its rapid onset, reversibility, and high prevalence in undiagnosed or poorly controlled diabetes—especially in physically active individuals who may skip meals or mis-time insulin. Traumatic brain injury is highly plausible given the occupational setting and mechanism (unwitnessed collapse); even without reported head strike, acceleration-deceleration forces or fall-related intracranial hemorrhage can cause delayed deterioration. Ischemic stroke ranks third: construction workers face elevated cardiovascular risk (hypertension, dehydration, exertion), and posterior circulation strokes may present with fluctuating consciousness and minimal focal signs initially. Postictal altered mental status is common after generalized seizures, particularly if unwitnessed or brief; absence of reported convulsions does not exclude seizure. Carbon monoxide poisoning is strongly considered because construction sites frequently use gas-powered tools in poorly ventilated areas (trenches, trailers, garages), and CO causes headache, dizziness, syncope, and confusion—often with cherry-red skin absent and co-workers potentially asymptomatic or overlooked. Less likely diagnoses (e.g., opioid overdose, meningitis, hepatic encephalopathy) are excluded by lack of supporting history (no known substance use, no fever/meningismus, no liver disease) and lower pretest probability in this demographic and setting."}
